note.happening: Meta rose 3.4% to 609.89. That put it just under a resistance zone from 611.95 to 626.54, a price band where rallies have stalled before. The stock is still in a downtrend, below its 50-day average of 672.4 and its 200-day average of 626.86. No news has come in since the last note. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: Demand looks solid. Sales grew 27.53% over the last twelve months, to 241.6B from 189.5B. Growth is slowing, though: sales grew 26.07% year over year last quarter, down from 33.08% two quarters ago. Profitability is the real problem. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 28.6B from 44.8B. R&D takes 31.68% of revenue. The company now holds slightly more debt than cash (net cash -1.2B, total debt 83.7B), but it has 82.4B of liquidity, so funding is not the risk. The filings data also says the company missed forecasts last quarter by 29% and that profit per share is lagging sales. The mix of rising spending and shrinking cash flow fits a heavy investment cycle (general knowledge), but the reports do not yet show that spending paying off. Two items affect only sentiment and governance, not the business: insiders sold $14.1M outside pre-set plans, and the tech market is in a downtrend with elevated fear. At risk: margins and cash generation. Not at risk: demand, the 81.03% gross margin, and the ability to pay debts.

worth.text: The methods disagree a lot. The discounted cash flow model (DCF), which values the company on its future cash, starts from today's reduced free cash flow of 28.6B and gives 244.22 (bear), 379.4 (base) and 517.42 (bull). All three are below the 609.89 price. To justify 609.89, cash flow would need to start growing at 36.7% a year. That is above the fastest growth figure the model uses as a starting point, last year's 28% sales growth. Even at 30% starting growth the model gives 477.73. The other method compares the price with Meta's own past price-to-sales ratios and gives a much higher range: 475.85 at the low end, 707.21 in the middle and 881.21 at the high end. At 6.5 times sales, the stock is at the 37th percentile of its own 5-year range and close to the peer median of 6.0. Its trailing P/E, the price divided by the last year's earnings per share, is 20.9. The gap between the methods comes down to one thing: whether 28.6B is the new normal for free cash flow or a low point in a spending cycle. If margins slip further, to a 24% operating margin, the DCF value drops to 245.02. My range runs from the low end of the sales history to its middle.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.
